steps.body: Count dots one at a time. Touch each dot once. The **last** number you say tells **how many**!

widget.prompt: Tap dots into the frame until there are 4.

commonCounts.feedback: That is 5 dots. Count again — stop at 4.
Only 3 so far. One more makes 4.

widget.missFeedback: Count each dot as you tap: 1, 2, 3, 4.
widget.successFeedback: Yes! Four dots. The last number says how many.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents count objects.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for count objects must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines count objects.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: Say one number for each dot: 1, 2, 3. Never skip a dot. Never count one twice.

explanationVariants: Count each dot once: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The last number, 5, tells how many.
Touch and count to the last dot: 5.

widget.prompt: Dots will flash. How many did you see?

commonPicks.feedback: So close — one more dot was hiding. It was 5.
That is one too many. Count the flash again: 5.

widget.successFeedback: Yes — 5! You saw it like a dice face.

commonCounts.feedback: That is 8 — one too many. Stop at 7.

widget.successFeedback: Seven dots! A full row of 5 and 2 more.

explanationVariants: Count the dots one by one: there are 3.

commonPicks.feedback: One dot got missed. There were 3.
One extra got counted. There were 3.

explanationVariants: When you count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, the last number — 6 — is how many there are.
The last number said tells the amount: 6.

widget.prompt: Maya counts her toys: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. How many toys does she have?

options.feedback: 1 was the first number. The LAST number, 6, tells how many.
Yes! The last number counted tells how many: 6 toys.
She kept going past 5 — the last number was 6.
She stopped at 6, so there are 6 toys.

explanationVariants: Moving the same six dots does not add or remove any. The count stays 6.
The spacing changed, but the amount did not. There are still 6 dots.

widget.prompt: Six dots were counted, then only moved into a scattered pattern. Without adding or removing any, how many must flash?

commonPicks.feedback: Moving dots did not remove one. The same 6 dots remain.
Moving dots did not add one. The same 6 dots remain.

widget.missFeedback: Only the spacing changed. No dot was added or removed, so the count stays 6.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — still 6. Moving the dots changes their spacing, not how many there are.

hints: Ask what changed: only the spaces between the dots.
No dot was added. No dot was taken away.
The starting count was 6, so the ending count is also 6.

steps.body: Count each thing once. The last number tells how many.
takeaways: Touch and count: one number for each thing.
The last number said is how many there are.
Scattered or in a row — the count stays the same.

concept.body: Count one number for each dot. Do not skip. Do not repeat. The last number tells how many.

commonPicks.feedback: One more was there. Count again: 4.
That is one too many. It was 4.
